verdict.rationale: Godot documents its own first-party programming interfaces: an object-oriented API in GDScript, C# on the modern .NET runtime, and C++/GDExtension. These count as the product's official SDK surface for building against the engine. Caveats are real: C# needs a separate .NET editor download, and community users report C# is second-class and cannot export to the web. Missing for 10: explicit packaged or versioned SDK distribution documentation, parity across language bindings, C# web export, and independent corroboration of SDK maturity beyond GDScript.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Keep your code modular with an object-oriented API using Godot's own GDScript, C#, C++, or bring your own using GDExtension.
In Godot, it is implemented with the modern .NET runtime.
to enable C# support for your project you need to download a .NET version of the editor from the Godot website.
